content: The dissertation says that for much of the next five years, until his death in Herat in 835/1432, Ibn Turka wandered through northern and north-western Iran seeking livelihood, teaching hadith and tafsir and writing treatises for governors; his surviving letters from then are largely pleas for clemency or for help, and he sought patronage especially at the Marʿashī court in Mazandaran and the Karkiya court in Gilan.
